public_rationale: The financing sequence does not establish $10 billion of cash burn. Later reporting puts full-year 2025 burn at $8 billion, which strongly challenges the inference but measures a different period. Without matching cash-flow records, the two-month assertion cannot be scored supported or contradicted under the period-matching rule.
limitations: The available figures are press reports, not accessible cash-flow statements.
Annual net cash burn cannot automatically be allocated to individual months.
Neither plausible interpretation of the two-month window has a matching measurement.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI appears to have burned at least ten billion dollars in the two months before this August 2025 post.

statement.excerpt: So, as a reminder, OpenAI appears to have burned at least ten billion dollars in the last two months.

our_interpretation: Burned means net cash consumed by the business, excluding financing inflows, rather than money raised, total expenditure, or accounting losses.
The literal two-month window is June 6 through August 6, 2025. The surrounding references to June and August financing also permit an approximate June–July reading.
The estimate accounting basis reflects his inference from cited press reporting about financing.
Appears qualifies confidence but does not erase the numerical assertion.
criteria.support_condition: Reliable cash-flow records establish at least $10 billion of net business cash consumption during the stated two-month window.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish less than $10 billion of net business cash consumption during that window.

evidence.explanation: Sources report annual cash burn below the amount claimed for two months. This is material countercontext, but an annual net total does not establish the result for a particular subperiod without its cash-flow breakdown.
